steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). If you don't have a 10-inch oven-proof skillet, lightly grease a 7x11-inch baking dish.
Place bacon in a large oven-proof skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels. Crumble and set aside.
Whisk eggs, milk, melted butter, salt, and pepper together in a bowl; pour into oven-proof skillet or prepared baking dish. Sprinkle with green onions and crumbled bacon. Cover with Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.description: Make this classic frittata with eggs, bacon, and cheese, or try other variations with any add-ins you like for a satisfying brunch or meal anytime.

review.reviewBody: Five stars for taste, ease of preparation and aesthetic appeal. So versatile! Add whatever you might put in an omelet or scrambled eggs. Great way to use up vegetables in the fridge too! In this case I browned the bacon, drained most of the grease, added finely chopped multi-colored bell peppers and onions, briefly sauteed that, then added it to my beaten eggs (which I just mixed with salt and pepper and half-and-half) along with some sliced black olives and garden fresh chives. I baked it in a pretty, shallow buttered casserole. No muss, no fuss, free to do other things while it baked, and it cut into individual servings perfectly. This will definitely be a re-do.
Instead of baking, I just use a covered frypan on the stove on medium high heat, comes out beautiful!

This is a terrifically simple and easily modifiable recipe. I doubled the eggs (12) used 1 1/2 cups milk, I had Costco precooked bacon and only used about six slices, because I was also serving uncured bacon on the side. I used about a 1/2 cup of ricotta cheese, a small zucchini, about 2 tbsps. of melted butter, green onion, and 1/8 cup of shredded cheddar cheese on top. The result was a lighter and taller frittata in a #10 (large) cast iron skillet. It easily served a table of 7 and there wasn't a bite left over. I served with bacon, hashbrowns, fruit salad with a smidge of honey & mint, and pancakes. I'd love to make it again with Gruyere cheese and mushrooms!

I didn't use a skillet; instead, I used a muffin pan with paper inserts (to keep them from sticking to the pan) for "personal" frittatas that I ended up freezing. I also used crumbled ground sausage rather than bacon, a chopped onion, and a chopped green pepper. Came out delicious

I'm from the South and our motto is Why Use Butter When You Have Bacon Grease? After cooking the bacon, I tossed in some onions and peppers, sauteed them until they were soft, added the eggs and baked according to the recipe. It turned out perfect! I did not need the salt because the bacon grease cintained all the salt I needed. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

I added 1 extra piece of bacon, 2 extra eggs, used heavy whipping cream (3/4cup) instead of milk, and sautéed some onions, tomato, and spinach in bacon grease and added it to the eggs along with the other ingredients. This recipe is so easy and delicious. I will definitely be making it again.

We really liked this. I cheated a little by using some HEB fully cooked bacon. I also substituted some diced white onion, instead of the green onions because that’s what I had on hand and, I threw in some diced jalapeño for some heat. I made it in my Mom’s old 8” cast iron skillet and, it turned out great. We’re having it again this week.

This recipe is easy and delicious. I used honey ham instead of bacon, spinach and 1 less egg. I cooked 30mins and an extra 15mins because it was still jiggly in the middle. Add Parmesan cheese on top after cooking! So good!

We really liked this recipe, I kept all of the basic original ingredients the same with the exception of leaving out the salt. I doubled the recipe and made it three times using standard sized muffin cups, those cook in about 18 minutes and I used sausage and ham in two batches and mushrooms and spinach in one, I'll be keeping this recipe to make multiple times. I froze all of the individual portions for future breakfasts.

I used shredded Gruyere instead of Cheddar and the whole family LOVED IT. I also added two more eggs (maybe mine were on the small side) and it took more like 40 minutes to bake. Such a simple recipe but so delicious!
Made with ham instead of bacon. I sautéed the ham with onion and peppers in a cast iron skillet. Baked in that same skillet.
I made it my own and added some other ingredients.
Easy and good. Thank you.
Super simple! I’ll make it every week!
Loved this recipe, had several ask for the recipe. I didn’t have the same veggies so substituted for spinach and tomatos but it came out great.
Looked and tasted fantastic. This recipe is awesome!
Delicious 😋 I had to keep mine in for 35 minutes. I used a ton of seasonings and frozen bell peppers and onions (put in with my butter to thaw before adding to the mix). Thank you!

When making this recipe, I was short on shredded cheddar cheese, so I opted to incorporate grated Parmesan cheese into the egg mixture and then with what shredded cheddar cheese I had left, I sprinkled over the top. It was amazing and everyone loved it. My mother in law is 86 and doesn’t care for many new recipes I whip up… she loved it and will be having it again!
I have not made a fritatta in years and had lost my recipe. This was awesome. Added 2 eggs, ham, green onions, parsley. Delish.
